title: Number of Music Playlists
summary: Given n distinct songs, determine the count of playlists that can be made to play at least goal songs, with each song played at least once and a song repeated only after k other songs have been played, modulo 10^9 + 7.
statement: Given n distinct songs, determine the count of playlists that can be made to play at least goal songs, with each song played at least once and a song repeated only after k other songs have been played, modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: A playlist has goal positions chosen from n distinct songs and must use every song.
A song may repeat only after at least k other songs have played.
Return the number of playlists modulo 1000000007.
hints: Track playlist length and number of distinct songs already used.
Append a new song in n-used ways, or replay one of used-k eligible songs.
Accumulate both transitions modulo the limit.
The last position is uniquely new or repeated, so the transitions partition all valid playlists.
editorial: The last position is uniquely new or repeated, so the transitions partition all valid playlists.

tests.explanation: All six permutations use every song once and satisfy the repeat rule.
After both songs appear, either may repeat, giving six valid playlists.
